record.original_question: Develop effective invariants and, if possible, a classification theory for welded knots. In particular, determine whether Satoh's map from welded knots or links to ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space is faithful, and determine whether a welded knot with trivial fundamental group must itself be trivial as a welded knot.

evidence.quote: The question is to construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, to classify them.
Is this Satoh mapping faithful from equivalence classes of welded knots (links) to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space?
If a welded knot has trivial fundamental group, does this imply that the knot is trivial as a welded knot?

artifact.category_tag: Welded knots and ribbon torus embeddings
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A virtual knot diagram is an immersed closed curve in the plane whose only singularities are double points, each labelled either as a classical crossing (with over/under information) or as a virtual crossing (drawn as a small circle, with no over/under information). Welded knots are equivalence classes of virtual knot diagrams under planar isotopy and the following local moves:
- the three classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3 (applied to classical crossings);
- the three virtual Reidemeister moves V1, V2, V3 (analogues of R1, R2, R3 in which all crossings involved are virtual);
- the mixed move M (a strand carrying only virtual crossings may be slid past a classical crossing);
- the forbidden overcrossing move F1: an overstrand may pass through a virtual crossing.
(The other "forbidden" move, F2, in which an understrand passes through a virtual crossing, is NOT allowed.)

A ribbon torus-knot is a smooth embedding T : S^1 × S^1 → R^4 (or S^4) which bounds an immersed solid torus B^2 × S^1 → R^4 whose only self-intersections are so-called ribbon singularities (transverse double disks each of whose preimages consists of one disk in the interior of B^2 × S^1 and one disk meeting the boundary in a circle). Ribbon torus-knots are considered up to ambient isotopy of R^4.

Satoh's tube construction associates to every welded knot K a ribbon torus-knot Tube(K) ⊂ R^4, well defined up to ambient isotopy, by tubing the underlying virtual diagram. This induces a well-defined surjective map
   Tube : { welded knots } / equivalence  →  { ribbon torus-knots } / ambient isotopy.

The fundamental group of a welded knot K is the group π_1(K) defined by the Wirtinger presentation read from any virtual diagram representing K (with one generator per classical arc and one Wirtinger relation per classical crossing); this is invariant under welded equivalence, and π_1(unknot) ≅ Z.

Problems.

(a) Construct a complete (or otherwise effective) system of invariants for welded knots that can be used to classify them up to welded equivalence.

(b) Determine whether Satoh's tube map
   Tube : { welded knots } / equivalence  →  { ribbon torus-knots } / ambient isotopy
is injective (faithful). Equivalently: if two welded knots K_1, K_2 satisfy Tube(K_1) ≅ Tube(K_2) as ribbon torus-knots in R^4, must K_1 and K_2 be equivalent as welded knots? The same question is asked for welded links and ribbon torus-links.

(c) Determine whether a welded knot K with π_1(K) ≅ Z is necessarily welded-equivalent to the trivial welded knot.
artifact.status_search_result: The faithfulness of Satoh's tube map and the question of whether a welded knot with infinite cyclic fundamental group must be trivial are still discussed as open problems in recent literature on welded knots and ribbon torus-knots (e.g., 2024 work on non-triviality of welded knots and ribbon torus-knots, and 2021 work on generalizations of Satoh's tube map). No proof of injectivity, nor a counterexample for either question, appears to be established. A full classification of welded knots is also not available.

status_evidence.title: Non-triviality of welded knots and ribbon torus-knots
status_evidence.snippet: Studies non-triviality detection for welded knots and the ribbon torus-knots they map to under Satoh's tube map.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work continues to investigate non-triviality of welded knots and ribbon torus-knots, indicating these questions remain active.

status_evidence.title: Some generalizations of Satoh's Tube map
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses local moves under which the Tube map is invariant, addressing the injectivity question.
status_evidence.claim: The injectivity (faithfulness) of Satoh's tube map is treated as an open question being approached via new local moves.

status_evidence.title: On the welded Tube map
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates properties of the tube map from welded knotted objects to ribbon tori/spheres.
status_evidence.claim: Faithfulness of the welded tube map remains an outstanding question in the literature.
